angle: DL/EDGE: pass-rush drill burst and Run-the-Hoop bend (Hoop G) vs NFL get-off and pressure rate; year-standardized; yardstick = no-tracking forecast (pick, weight, EDGE share, NGS score, official 10-yd split and 3-cone) fit leave-one-class-out, plus ridge, time-forward and pick-and-role-only versions
metric_name: Hoop G: hardest 0.5 s of sideways acceleration (g) on the Run-the-Hoop lap, z within Combine year; used as a day-3/undrafted shortlist (top third of class)
headline_number: Day-3/undrafted pool only: shortlist 8 of 15 (53%) beat the out-of-class no-tracking pressure forecast vs 8 of 32 (25%); gap +28 points (90% Newcombe 4 to 50), Bayesian P(gap>0) 97%, within-class relabelling p 0.037, ahead in 3 of 3 classes; time-forward version +20 (-8 to 47). Drill burst reaches NFL first-second burst (partial rho 0.27, 0.62 noise-corrected) and get-off predicts pressure (0.35), but drill burst to pressure is 0.06 (-0.14 to 0.26).
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round 13 cand_1 (8.11) with a new lean script (about 1 minute instead of 10+) and the round-13 judges' transferable top_changes: one pool stated once in the lede (day-3/undrafted), with the weakness (time-forward) in the lede; a 5-row robustness table (primary, ridge, time-forward, pick-and-role-only yardstick as the regression-to-the-mean check, drop best rusher) with player-level Newcombe intervals; a Bayesian posterior for the gap; the get-off angle rebuilt as a drill-to-game chain with partial correlations after weight and role, restricted to linemen with 8+ sampled random rushes, and a reliability-disattenuated drill-to-game correlation; NGS season get-off added as an outcome; Holm, beta-binomial, hash and calibration detail cut; motivation rewritten; new decision case where drill and tape disagree on a large sample (Jaylen Harrell, 461 rushes) and the rule's false negative (Isaiah McGuire); figures redrawn for column width (2x2 lap grid with 11-12 pt readouts on one colour scale, chain figure with grouped headers, scatter of all scored rushers); 1,813 words by check.py, 1,994 by wc -w; 4 figures + 4 tables.
open_risks: The shortlist rule was written after earlier rounds saw the Hoop G slope; Hoop G was the best of 14 screened drill-outcome pairs (search-adjusted p 0.10); only the 2026 class is a clean test.
Time-forward evaluation is weaker: 5 of 11 vs 5 of 20, gap +20 points with an interval crossing zero.
Small counts (15 vs 32) and a Hoop G reliability estimated from only 10 linemen with two runs (0.37).
Drill burst correlates with NFL first-second burst on sampled frames (0.27) but not with NGS season get-off directly (-0.09), so the first link of the burst chain is fragile.
No visible in-game mechanism for Hoop G (first-second burst 0.07, 1.5 s depth 0.04); scheme reads come from loop rates on about 20 sampled rushes.
